question: How should a copied icon's SVG code reach a code editor or a plain text box?
context: Copy now puts a drawing on the clipboard as a picture and as an SVG file. Chrome-based apps can read the SVG file; code editors, plain text boxes and Safari read only text, and the text slot already carries the measurement list when a drawing has measurements.

options.label: Copy Merged also pastes the SVG code as text
options.summary: Shift Command C on a drawing puts the SVG code on as text too. Pasting into a code editor or any plain text box gives the code. A drawing with measurements on it pastes the measurement list there instead, as today.
pros: One copy pastes the picture into a chat, shapes into Figma and code into an editor
cons: Every plain text box gets the code, including a plain chat box or a terminal
A drawing with measurements never pastes its code anywhere
options.mitigation: Screenshots and photos carry no SVG, so a redline on a screenshot pastes exactly as today.

options.label: A Copy SVG row in Edit and in right-click
options.summary: A new Copy SVG row sits under Copy Merged in Edit and in the right-click menu of a layer, a frame and the canvas. It puts the SVG code on as text. Copy and Copy Merged keep the text slot for the measurement list.
pros: What Photoshop does (right-click a layer, Copy SVG) and what Figma does (Copy as SVG)
Nothing changes in a chat or a plain text box unless you ask for code
cons: One more row to find, and no key for it
options.mitigation: It sits right under Copy Merged and on the right-click of the thing it copies, where a Photoshop user looks first.

options.label: Leave it: code editors use Export
options.summary: Copy keeps the picture and the SVG file type only. To get the code into an editor, export the SVG and open the file.
cons: The icon epic promise of copying the SVG holds only for Chrome-based apps
options.mitigation: Export already writes the identical file.
